evidence.summary: 在 DSH 中持续运行研究项目、计算实验、编写论文，并以独立评审和版本检查约束交付。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

owner注册的项目操作经JSON行RPC送Python domain，返回id必须匹配；helper关闭或协议错误会拒绝pending请求。默认bootstrap校验伴随wheel摘要，用独立缓存与flock完成venv/pip安装，再启动ark.orchestrator.native_domain；pack.py从同一仓库固定源码打入ark与资源，故该Python代码是本组件的直接打包依赖，不将整个ARK都算成DSH组件规模。

实验入口封存计划与脚本摘要，已封存代码变化会拒绝轮询或要求新的结果路径，native_experiment用收据和后端identity恢复同一操作。完成测量、编译、评审与交付分别有状态；恢复不意味着重算，也不证明旧材料适用于新模型或宿主。

只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

统计范围仅integrations/dsh；为核实直接打包依赖，定向读取同固定提交ark/orchestrator/native_domain.py、ark/compute/native_experiment.py和ark/review.py，不把ARK全仓规模算作组件规模。
组件为integrations/dsh独立bundle。pack.py构建同仓库领域wheel并内嵌manifest；本次未下载发布tarball比较，不声称发布包与源码已实测一致。

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 指定DSH版本与原profile/model | 必需 | 挂载和持久会话恢复 | 版本或模型不符拒绝恢复 |
| Linux、flock、Node对应版本 | 本研究使用条件 | 项目锁与宿主执行 | 其他平台兼容未知 |
| Python≥3.10、venv/pip | 必需 | 启动同版本领域wheel | bootstrap失败不发布ready缓存 |
| Docker与实验镜像 | 默认本地实验需要 | 受限worker运行 | 无法提交本地计算 |
| TeX Live、BibTeX | 论文交付需要 | 编译当前PDF | 无有效编译不交付 |
| 模型账号、必要时图像能力 | 模型流程需要 | owner/reviewer及视觉检查 | 无法完成相应检查 |
| Slurm/Apptainer、Gemini服务 | 特定操作才需要 | 集群实验或深度研究/配图 | 本地小计算试用可先不用 |

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次使用 | wheel依赖、镜像与TeX磁盘/下载，金额未知 | 建专用profile、配置模型和原环境 | 尚无本轮安装耗时 |
| 持续使用 | owner、reviewer模型调用和实验计算 | 读实验/论文、处理未签署评审 | 默认owner时限不等于费用上限 |
| 失败恢复 | 可能仍占用的容器/Slurm任务、重编译 | 保留项目与原DSH home，核对收据后恢复 | stopped不保证后端终止 |
| 退出 | 需要保留论文、原始结果和审计记录的存储 | 停实验、核对后端后卸bundle | 卸载不代替停止未确认作业 |
先在专用Linux/DSH profile中用本地Docker核对一个结果可人工复算的小任务，不立即接集群或昂贵外部服务。检查改稿后旧评审失效、原会话恢复与停止后容器实际状态；若证据不能解释结论或后端仍未决，就停止自动执行并保留材料退回手工实验审阅。依据见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
|---|---|---|
| 连续研究 | 同owner会话与固定模型检查点 | 长任务最终合格率 |
| 结果可追溯 | 脚本计划封存、测量摘要与当前稿门槛 | 科学推论是否正确 |
| 独立评审 | 非seeded子会话与证据回执校验 | 模型判断的独立错误率 |
| 停止恢复 | Docker身份核对与取消记录 | Slurm未决状态终止时间与实效 |
[Q02](#research-q02) 的固定运行时会话、封存脚本与打包wheel摘要，以及[Q03](#research-q03) 的revision绑定评审值得研究工作流借鉴。移植需承担RPC、依赖缓存、后端状态对账与评审规则维护，不能把项目状态视为外部副作用证明。
[Q01](#research-q01) 与 [Q02](#research-q02) 支持把持久会话、封存实验与同版本独立评审串成可恢复项目；[Q03](#research-q03) 展示deliver确实重新检查文件和回执。贡献在交付责任和证据生命周期的组合，不是科学推理正确性保证。
[Q03](#research-q03) 显示最重要的两种边界：结构化评审仍可能误读科学证据；项目stopped也不证明所有Slurm操作已终止。采用必须把论文有效性与外部副作用逐项核对，不能只看成功状态。
[Q05](#research-q05) 提出尚未验证的终止证明设计：将项目已停与每项后端已确认终止分别展示，避免把 Slurm 的 cancelling 或 submission_unknown 状态误当作资源已释放。先用提交回执丢失、取消仍活跃和查询失败做对照；若不能减少误报或明显增加无收益负担，就应停止该方向。

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 固定会话、脚本封存与[Q03](#research-q03)版本评审不是单入口包装，novelty/mechanism各50%；原生DSH和领域包继承能力不归为原创，缺少直接替代同条件反例不足75%；这些证据生命周期办法可迁移但未验证，transferability50%；多个生命周期在统一项目串接simplification50%。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 从临时聊天改为持续owner和独立reviewer，workflow50%；交付单位由文章变为当前稿/测量/评审一致的记录，delivery50%；[Q04](#research-q04)多项环境前提仍在，仅便利现有研究者reach25%；未改变计费资源交易结构economics0，而非将未知账单记0。

recommendation.reason: 具备 Linux、固定 DSH 与 Docker 经验的研究开发者，可在专用 profile 试一个结果可人工精确核对的小计算问题。相比临时聊天加手工交接，它把同一项目的测量、论文和评审版本串成可恢复的交付链，源码支持这一机制增量。若原始证据无法解释结论、停止后仍有未决任务或修订超出预算，应先核对并停止后端，再保留材料退回手工实验与审阅。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) README:5-11与index:560-603对应研究者重复的实验/论文/评审交接，超过一般用途明确50%；能解释此类人群的重复摩擦取75%，无真实持续需求/用户负担数据不足100%。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) index:158-170、native_domain:890-910及[Q03](#research-q03)3118-3158体现恢复和版本硬约束，比脚本聊天多实质交付机制取75%，超过仅潜力50%；科学判断与停止边界未排查且无同条件效果，不能100%。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 跟到RPC、Python领域与打包映射，[Q03](#research-q03) 跟到实际worker、取消和deliver分支，核心受控本地试用链覆盖超过片段25%；只读源码未运行，取50%上限不取75%。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04) README:9-11和bootstrap:26-54有多层配置/下载/模型复核负担，stop不确定分支需人工处理，取25%；存在原项目保留/本地Docker核对与手工退路故高于无法恢复0%，但负担不足50%可称相称。

publication.summaries.text: 在 DSH 中持续运行研究项目、计算实验、编写论文，并以独立评审和版本检查约束交付。

items.模型工具: 受限项目操作、实验、论文编译、独立评审与交付
items.事件监听: 投影owner/reviewer持久会话事件并轮询停止/指令

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| run/resume | 建立与继续同一研究项目 | 原DSH版本、模型、会话与项目锁 |
| status | 查询持久状态与证据路径 | 不等于原始结果已科学验证 |
| stop | 记录停止意图并取消跟踪实验 | stopped不保证Slurm未决操作已终止 |
| 计划与实验 | 封存脚本/计划后运行受限worker | Docker或配置后端，结果由收据核对 |
| 项目文件编辑与编译 | 写稿、生成当前PDF并校验 | TeX环境及项目操作边界 |
| 独立评审 | 冻结证据后由隔离子会话检查 | 模型仍可能误读，不代替科学审阅 |
| deliver | 校验当前稿/结果/review并记录交付 | 任一blocker或陈旧材料拒绝 |

publication.advice.text: 先在专用Linux/DSH profile中用本地Docker核对一个结果可人工复算的小任务，不立即接集群或昂贵外部服务。检查改稿后旧评审失效、原会话恢复与停止后容器实际状态；若证据不能解释结论或后端仍未决，就停止自动执行并保留材料退回手工实验审阅。依据见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

      "path": "integrations/dsh/README.md",
      "content": "# Idea2Paper for DeepSeek Harness\n\n[中文](README_zh.md)\n\nGive Idea2Paper a question and a new project directory. A persistent DSH session plans the experiment, runs it, reads the measurements and writes the paper. An independent reviewer examines the manuscript and can request original results and rendered pages. Follow up with the same project to change the experiment or repair a claim.\n\n## Install the prerelease\n\nThis source build supports two DSH runtimes on Linux with pnpm. Use Node.js 22.12 or newer for DSH 0.2.1-rc.2, and Node.js 24.9 or newer for DSH 0.2.2-rc.5. Resume each project with its original DSH version and profile. [DSH 0.2.1-rc.2](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh/v/0.2.1-rc.2) · [DSH 0.2.2-rc.5](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh/v/0.2.2-rc.5)\n\nPython 3.10 or newer with venv and pip, TeX Live with pdflatex and BibTeX, and a working Docker daemon are needed for the local experiment. The first run installs the bundled Python wheel and its dependencies into a private cache and builds the experiment image. Budget disk space and package-download time for that setup.\n\nInstall version 0.2.0-alpha.29 into a dedicated profile with one command. The DSH Web Discover view requires the full upstream CLI with its Web profile.\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile idea2paper add https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/releases/download/dsh-bundle-0.2.0-alpha.29/idea2paper-dsh-0.2.0-alpha.29.tgz\n```\n\nTo install a local build, run these commands from the source checkout.\n\n```sh\npython3 integrations/dsh/pack.py --out dist/dsh\nversion=$(node -p \"require('./integrations/dsh/package.json').version\")\ndsh plugin --profile idea2paper add \"$PWD/dist/dsh/idea2paper-dsh-$version.tgz\"\ndsh --profile idea2paper --help\n```\n\nTo see how a review changes across manuscript revisions, open the offline replay. It contains three PDFs, their reviewer findings and the measured rows. The archive reproduces the example first published with alpha.3 and requires no model key. [Download the review replay](https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/releases/download/dsh-bundle-0.2.0-alpha.24/review-replay.zip)\n\n## Run a small study\n\nConfigure your chosen model in DSH. For its DeepSeek provider, set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the environment that launches DSH. Use a model and provider with image input for checks requiring inspection of rendered figures. A standalone project with a configured Gemini key can also request Google Deep Research and method illustrations. Those calls use the associated provider account.\n\n```sh\ndsh --profile idea2paper run search-study \"Compare the number of key inspections in linear and binary search for missing targets on sorted arrays. Include small arrays and report the exact counts.\"\ndsh --profile idea2paper status search-study\ndsh --profile idea2paper resume search-study \"Report the crossover and any ties in the tested range.\"\ndsh --profile idea2paper stop search-study\ndsh --profile idea2paper resume search-study\n```\n\nIn a terminal, status shows the Slurm job, illustration check, last compiled body length and reviewed edition when available. Use `status <project> --json` or redirect its output for the full status record.\n\nThe first command opens the project. Run status, send a follow-up or request a stop from another terminal. Resume after an interruption with the original profile, model and project directory. Standalone runs default to local experiment execution. A configured Slurm environment can dispatch experiments to the cluster. The paper must pass the current revision's review and delivery checks.\n\n| Inspect | Project file |\n| --- | --- |\n| Scientific milestones and measured artifact paths | `auto_research/state/research_events.jsonl` |\n| Measurements and plotted figures | `results/` and `paper/figures/` |\n| Rendered paper | `paper/main.pdf` |\n| Independent verdict and issue evidence | `auto_research/state/native_review.json` |\n| Archived reviewed PDFs | `auto_research/state/reviews/<revision>/main.pdf` |\n| Delivery checks | `auto_research/state/delivery_report.yaml` |\n\nThe researcher can plot measured JSON columns directly as lines, points or grouped bars. A custom plotting script reads `/study/results.json` and saves its named output in `/output/`. For comparisons, Nano Banana supplies the study artwork and the tool typesets the experimental conditions from the approved plan. Each passing panel includes its caption. Mechanism diagrams are also available. During revisions, the owner can edit the numbered lines it has read. The editor checks changes to a previously compiled manuscript with TeX before saving them.\n\nOpen the manuscript progress recording to follow four real drafts from 0.91 to 3.34 body pages against a four-page target. Select a bar to return to its compilation event. The host shows page coverage independently of the review verdict. [Watch the dashboard replay](https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/releases/download/dsh-bundle-0.2.0-alpha.24/draft-length.webm)\n\n### Independent review\n\nA reviewer working with a verified results table can commit its proposed comparison, competing explanation and discriminating observation before it reads the paper. It can search a phrase in the rendered PDF and compare the language across sections. In the hosted dashboard, open a judgment to see its evidence or send the researcher a question about the quoted page.\n\nIn a four-page study, a reviewer accepted a mechanism that the submitted measurements did not establish. Read its cited evidence before relying on a scientific judgment.\n\nWhen a revised experiment returns the same measured rows, the reviewer first sees the original question and the measurement schema. It writes a short Python reproduction for one recorded condition. The bundle freezes that program before opening the manuscript, worker source and results in the same reviewer session. The review records each recomputed value alongside the worker’s value. If the data or compute is unavailable, the review identifies the missing evidence.\n\nIn the dashboard, expand **What the reviewer checked → Experimental controls** to inspect the comparison. The local Docker or configured Apptainer science image runs the calculation offline. A Slurm project can perform this check without submitting another job.\n\n## Discover\n\nIn DSH Web, open **Plugins → More → Experimental plugins**, enable **Custom plugin markets**, and select **Discover → Add index source**. Add the community preview index below once. Discover lists subsequent releases at this address and selects the version compatible with your DSH installation. The card identifies the exact release package commit and its supported DSH version. Market sources and installations belong to the selected profile. Use the CLI install command for the `idea2paper` profile when browsing from a separate Web profile. [DSH Discover guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.1-rc.2/docs/user/guide/plugin-market.md)\n\n```text\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaust-ark/ARK/dsh-bundle-preview/index.json\n```\n\n## Verify and publish\n\nFrom the source checkout, put the pinned DSH binary and pnpm on PATH. Build once and test the same tarball intended for release. Choose a new output directory for the distribution repository.\n\n```sh\npython3 integrations/dsh/pack.py --out dist/dsh\nversion=$(node -p \"require('./integrations/dsh/package.json').version\")\ngit clone --single-branch --branch dsh-bundle-preview https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK.git dist/dsh/channel\npython3 integrations/dsh/verify.py \"dist/dsh/idea2paper-dsh-$version.tgz\" --prepare dist/dsh/release --previous-index dist/dsh/channel/index.json\n```\n\nThe release check uses `pdflatex` and `bibtex`. With local model responses it drives the installed owner through run and resume, breaks a rendered citation and the page layout, and requires a new independent review of the repaired PDF. The test spends no model credits.\n\nTo qualify a completed four-page ICML research project against the editorial benchmark, keep the authenticated Google Deep Research response outside the project and run the following from the checkout.\n\n```sh\npython scripts/eval_manuscript.py editorial PROJECT --google-response INTERACTION.json --output acceptance.json\n```\n\nThe report verifies ten distinct source-backed publications in the body, the printed figures, references and appendix, final-column balance, a clean PDF rebuild and the review of that exact revision. The digits and Friedman benchmarks also replay their experimental measurements.\n\nThe verifier installs the archive over loopback into a clean profile, reads a stopped project using the packaged companion, checks the Git target in the running DSH Web Discover service, and installs that exact commit through a local Git mirror. Its separate Git repository contains the exact unpacked npm contents, including the wheel, and an index pointing to that package commit. The legacy v0.1.0-alpha.1 package fixture is available as `verify_legacy.py`.\n\nInclude the offline replay from alpha.3 and checksums for both downloads. The release tag exposes the Discover index as a raw HTTPS file.\n\n```sh\ncurl -fsSL https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/releases/download/dsh-bundle-0.2.0-alpha.3/review-replay.zip -o dist/dsh/review-replay.zip\n(cd dist/dsh && sha256sum idea2paper-dsh-${version}.tgz review-replay.zip > SHA256SUMS)\ngit -C dist/dsh/release push git@github.com:kaust-ark/ARK.git refs/tags/dsh-bundle-${version}\ngh release create dsh-bundle-${version} dist/dsh/idea2paper-dsh-${version}.tgz dist/dsh/review-replay.zip dist/dsh/SHA256SUMS --repo kaust-ark/ARK --verify-tag --prerelease --title \"Idea2Paper DSH ${version}\" --notes \"Persistent research sessions, measured experiments and revision-bound independent review. Supports DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.2-rc.5.\"\n```\n\nVerify the public tarball and Discover index against the tested files, then repeat the one-command installation with a fresh DSH home.\n\n```sh\ncurl -fsSL https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/releases/download/dsh-bundle-${version}/idea2paper-dsh-${version}.tgz -o dist/dsh/downloaded.tgz\ncmp dist/dsh/downloaded.tgz dist/dsh/idea2paper-dsh-${version}.tgz\ncurl -fsS https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaust-ark/ARK/dsh-bundle-${version}/index.json -o dist/dsh/downloaded-index.json\ncmp dist/dsh/downloaded-index.json dist/dsh/release/index.json\ncp dist/dsh/downloaded-index.json dist/dsh/channel/index.json\ngit -C dist/dsh/channel add index.json\ngit -C dist/dsh/channel commit -m \"List Idea2Paper $version in Discover\"\ngit -C dist/dsh/channel push origin HEAD:dsh-bundle-preview\n```\n\nAn npm maintainer can additionally publish the same archive with `npm publish dist/dsh/idea2paper-dsh-${version}.tgz --access public --tag alpha`. Check its registry `dist.integrity` before documenting the npm install path. To uninstall the profile plugin, run `dsh plugin --profile idea2paper remove idea2paper-dsh`. Keep the project directory and original profile for resuming work.\n"

      "content": "<p align=\"center\">\n  <strong>English</strong> • <a href=\"README_zh.md\">中文</a> • <a href=\"README_ar.md\">العربية</a>\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/logo_ark_transparent.png\" alt=\"idea2paper\" width=\"260\">\n</p>\n\n<h1 align=\"center\">idea2paper</h1>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <em>Offload the labour. Steer the science.</em>\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg\" alt=\"Python 3.10+\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-green.svg\" alt=\"Apache 2.0\">\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/actions/workflows/ci.yml\"><img src=\"https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg\" alt=\"CI\"></a>\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/agents-6-orange.svg\" alt=\"6 Agents\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/venues-20+-purple.svg\" alt=\"20+ Venues\">\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://idea2paper.org/\"><strong>Website</strong></a> •\n  <a href=\"#quick-start\">Quick Start</a> •\n  <a href=\"#requirements\">Requirements</a> •\n  <a href=\"#pipeline\">Pipeline</a> •\n  <a href=\"#agents\">Agents</a> •\n  <a href=\"#cloud-compute\">Cloud</a> •\n  <a href=\"#cli-reference\">CLI</a>\n</p>\n\n---\n\n<!-- docs:start -->\n\nidea2paper orchestrates **6 specialized AI agents** to turn a research idea into a paper — proposal analysis, literature search, Slurm experiments, LaTeX drafting, and iterative peer review — while you stay in control via **CLI**, **Dashboard**, or **Telegram**.\n\n```\nGive it an idea and a venue. idea2paper handles the rest.\n```\n\nThe fastest way to try it is the hosted instance at **[idea2paper.org](https://idea2paper.org/)** — sign in with your email, add one [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/keys) API key, and launch. A full paper with a budget model like DeepSeek typically bills **$10–25 of your own API credit**, depending on length — the dashboard shows the actual billed total per run. Self-hosting is a one-line install (below).\n\n## Papers Written by idea2paper\n\n<table align=\"center\">\n<tr>\n<td align=\"center\" width=\"33%\">\n<a href=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/papers/marco.pdf\"><img src=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/paper-marco.png\" alt=\"Budget-Constrained Multi-Modal Research Synthesis\" width=\"320\"></a>\n<br>\n<strong>Budget-Constrained Multi-Modal Research Synthesis via Iterative-Deepening Agentic Search</strong>\n<br>\n<sub>Template: EuroMLSys</sub>\n</td>\n<td align=\"center\" width=\"33%\">\n<a href=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/papers/heteroserve.pdf\"><img src=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/paper-heteroserve.png\" alt=\"HeteroServe\" width=\"320\"></a>\n<br>\n<strong>HeteroServe: Capability-Weighted Batch Scheduling for Heterogeneous GPU Clusters in LLM Inference</strong>\n<br>\n<sub>Template: ICML</sub>\n</td>\n<td align=\"center\" width=\"33%\">\n<a href=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/papers/tierkv.pdf\"><img src=\"https://idea2paper.org/assets/paper-tierkv.png\" alt=\"TierKV\" width=\"320\"></a>\n<br>\n<strong>TierKV: Prefetch-Aware Memory Tiering for KV Cache in LLM Serving</strong>\n<br>\n<sub>Template: NeurIPS</sub>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n---\n\n## Run inside DeepSeek Harness\n\nInstall the [Idea2Paper DSH bundle](integrations/dsh/README.md) into a dedicated profile. Each project keeps one research session across experiments, writing and revisions. The independent reviewer can inspect measured rows, original papers and rendered PDF pages. The guide includes the install command, prerequisites, and how to resume a project.\n\nWatch a reviewer finding arrive, open its source data, and inspect the exact PDF page under review. [Eight-second dashboard replay](https://github.com/kaust-ark/ARK/releases/download/dsh-bundle-0.2.0-alpha.20/reviewer-page.webm) · [Subscribe in DSH Discover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaust-ark/ARK/dsh-bundle-preview/index.json) · [Reviewer results and limitations](docs/dsh-review-example.md#reading-a-finding-on-the-dashboard)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://idea2paper.org/install.sh | bash\n```\n\nThe script:\n\n1. Detects your OS, installs miniforge if missing, builds the `ark-base` and `ark` conda envs, and installs idea2paper editable into `~/ARK` with the pinned DSH SDK.\n2. Asks for your API keys and an **email for dashboard login**. One **OpenRouter** key is the recommended setup — it unlocks every model plus deep research and figure generation; direct Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / DeepSeek keys also work. Press Enter to skip any.\n3. Installs the dashboard as a `systemd --user` service on port `9527` (use `--no-webapp` to opt out).\n4. Prints a one-time **magic-link URL** for your email — click it once and you're logged into the local dashboard. No SMTP, no Google OAuth.\n\nAfter that the dashboard at <http://localhost:9527> is the primary UX — create projects, set the model, run, monitor. The CLI also works:\n\n```bash\nark doctor          # verify install\nark new myproject   # interactive project wizard\nark run  myproject\nark monitor myproject\n```\n\nRe-run `ark webapp login <email>` anytime for a fresh sign-in link. Full installer flags: [`website/homepage/install.sh --help`](website/homepage/install.sh).\n\n### Start from an Existing PDF\n\n```bash\nark new myproject --from-pdf proposal.pdf\n```\n\nidea2paper parses the PDF with PyMuPDF + Claude Haiku, pre-fills the wizard, and kicks off from the extracted spec.\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n- **Python 3.10+** with `pyyaml` and `PyMuPDF`\n- **Agent runtime** runs on DeepSeek Harness (DSH) by default. Set `ARK_AGENT_RUNTIME=cli` to use the OpenHands CLI. Apptainer requires `ARK_AGENT_RUNTIME=sdk`.\n- **API key**: one [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/keys) key covers every model, deep research (Perplexity), and AI figures; single-vendor keys (Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / DeepSeek / …) work too but lose the pieces their vendor doesn't serve\n- **Optional**: LaTeX (`pdflatex` + `bibtex`), Slurm\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Manual Installation</strong></summary>\n\nThe fastest path is the one-line installer in [Quick Start](#quick-start). It runs the steps below for you and prints onboarding hints. To do it by hand:\n\n```bash\n# 1. Create the project research-stack template (no idea2paper code in here —\n#    each new project clones this env, so it must stay clean).\nconda env create -f environment.yml         # Linux (creates \"ark-base\")\n# OR for macOS:\nconda env create -f environment-macos.yml   # macOS (creates \"ark-base\")\n\n# 2. Install idea2paper itself into a SEPARATE env (not ark-base).\nconda create -n ark python=3.11 -y\nconda activate ark\npip install -e .                    # Core\npip install -e \".[research]\"       # + Gemini Deep Research & Nano Banana\npip install -e \".[webapp]\"         # + dashboard / systemd service support\n\n# 3. Optional OpenHands rollback runtime.\npip install uv && uv tool install --python 3.12 openhands\n\n# 4. Verify the selected runtime and API keys.\nark doctor\n```\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n## Framework\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"assets/framework.png\" alt=\"idea2paper framework\" width=\"900\">\n</p>\n\nidea2paper orchestrates three phases — **Initialization & Research**, **Iterative Development**, and **Iterative Review** — coordinated through shared memory, a persistent **Goal Anchor** re-injected into every agent call to prevent drift, and human-in-the-loop steering via the web dashboard or Telegram.\n\n---\n\n## Pipeline\n\nidea2paper runs three phases in sequence. The Review phase loops until the paper reaches the target score.\n\n| Phase | What Happens |\n|:------|:-------------|\n| **Research** | 5-step pipeline: Setup (conda env) → Analyze Proposal (researcher) → Deep Research (Perplexity via OpenRouter, or Gemini) → Specialization (researcher) → Bootstrap (skills & citations) |\n| **Dev** | Iterative experiment cycle: Plan Experiments → Run Experiments (Slurm or local) → Analyze Results → Evaluate Completeness |\n| **Review** | Compile → Review → Plan → Execute → Validate, repeating until score ≥ threshold |\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Review Loop details</strong></summary>\n\nEach iteration of the Review phase runs **5 steps**:\n\n| Step | Description |\n|:-----|:------------|\n| **Compile** | LaTeX → PDF, page count, page images |\n| **Review** | AI reviewer scores 1–10, lists Major & Minor issues |\n| **Plan** | Planner creates a prioritized action plan |\n| **Execute** | Researcher + Experimenter run in parallel; Writer revises LaTeX |\n| **Validate** | Verify changes compile; recompile PDF |\n\nThe loop repeats until the score reaches the acceptance threshold — or you intervene via Telegram.\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n## Agents\n\n| Agent | Role |\n|:------|:-----|\n| **Researcher** | Analyzes the proposal, runs the deep-research literature survey, and specializes agent prompts for the project |\n| **Reviewer** | Scores the paper against venue standards, generates improvement tasks |\n| **Planner** | Turns review feedback into a prioritized action plan; analyzes Dev-phase results |\n| **Writer** | Drafts and refines LaTeX sections with DBLP-verified references |\n| **Experimenter** | Designs experiments, submits Slurm jobs, analyzes results |\n| **Coder** | Writes and debugs experiment code and analysis scripts |\n\n---\n\n## Guardrails & Step Log\n\nAn autonomous run is watched and gated, not a black box.\n\n- **Live step log.** Every agent's actions — each bash command, file edit, and\n  result — stream into the log as they happen (no more 30-minute blank), and into\n  a structured `agent_steps.jsonl`. Secret values are redacted automatically.\n  Tune detail with `log_verbosity: quiet|normal|verbose|debug`.\n- **Pause-and-ask before the risky stuff.** Before deleting files, launching a\n  burst of jobs, provisioning a paid cloud instance, handling credentials,\n  pushing/exfiltrating data, or crossing a spend cap, idea2paper asks you on\n  **Telegram** and waits for approval (Approve / Deny / remember-this). It\n  remembers your answer so it doesn't re-ask, denies on timeout, and **fails open**\n  (auto-allows + logs) when no Telegram is configured — so nothing ever hangs.\n- **Idea gatekeeper (Gate A / Gate B).** Every submitted idea passes a\n  pre-launch ethics-and-soundness review (Gate A); after the literature survey\n  a novelty/scope check (Gate B) flags overlap with existing work and folds\n  honest scoping into the paper instead of overclaiming.\n- **Delivery checks.** Before a paper is delivered it is verified against an\n  explicit contract — disclosure present, every citation resolved, references\n  non-empty, generated figures actually used, page budget respected. The same\n  checks run standalone via `ark audit <project> [--repair]`.\n- **AI-use disclosure.** Every paper carries an acknowledgment that it was\n  produced with Idea2Paper and reviewed by the authors — inserted\n  automatically, for every venue.\n- **Two enforcement layers.** Shadow-PATH wrappers gate risky commands *before*\n  they run; a circuit breaker backstops anything that bypasses them. The\n  orchestrator's own autonomous cloud-provision / git-push / spend actions are\n  gated too — but commands you trigger yourself (`ark clear`, delete, stop) are not.\n\nConfigure it all under the `intervention:` block in\n[`config.example.yaml`](config.example.yaml); the default autonomy level\n(`standard`) only interrupts you for genuinely high-stakes actions.\n\n---\n\n## What Sets idea2paper Apart\n\n| | Other Tools | idea2paper |\n|---|:------------|:----|\n| **Control** | Fully autonomous — drifts from intent, no mid-run correction | Human-in-the-loop: pause at key decisions, steer via Telegram or web |\n| **Formatting** | Broken layouts, LaTeX errors, manual cleanup | Venue templates + sub-page length control to hit page limits exactly |\n| **Citations** | LLMs fabricate plausible-looking references | API-first BibTeX (DBLP / CrossRef / arXiv) with content–claim alignment |\n| **Review** | Text-only review of the LaTeX source | Visual-grounded: page images **and** source, scored against venue standards |\n| **Figures** | Default styles, wrong sizes, no page awareness | AI concept figures (PaperBanana) + venue-aware sizing: figures are saved at print size and never upscaled |\n| **Isolation** | Shared env — projects interfere with each other | Per-project conda env, sandboxed HOME, full multi-tenant isolation |\n| **Integrity** | LLMs simulate results instead of running real experiments | Anti-simulation prompts + builtin skills enforce real execution |\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Environment Isolation</strong></summary>\n\nEach project runs in its own **per-project conda environment**, cloned from a base env at project creation. This ensures full multi-tenant isolation:\n\n- **Sandboxed Python** — per-project `.env/` directory with its own packages\n- **Isolated HOME** — each orchestrator runs with `HOME` set to the project directory\n- **No cross-contamination** — `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` prevents leaking user-site packages\n- **Automatic provisioning** — `ark run` and the Web Portal detect and use the project conda env; the pipeline bootstraps it if missing\n\n```bash\n# The conda env is created automatically on first run.\n# ark run will detect and use it:\nark run myproject\n#   Conda env: /path/to/projects/myproject/.env\n```\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Skills System</strong></summary>\n\nidea2paper ships with **builtin skills** — modular instruction sets that agents load at runtime to enforce best practices:\n\n| Skill | Purpose |\n|:------|:--------|\n| **research-integrity** | Anti-simulation prompts: agents must run real experiments, not fabricate outputs |\n| **human-intervention** | Escalation protocol: agents pause and ask via Telegram before irreversible actions |\n| **env-isolation** | Enforces per-project environment boundaries |\n| **runtime-sandbox** | Locks each project to its own conda env, `HOME`, and tmp dir at runtime |\n| **figure-integrity** | Validates figure content matches data; prevents placeholder or hallucinated plots |\n| **page-adjustment** | Maintains page limits by adjusting content density, not deleting sections |\n\nSkills live in `skills/builtin/` and are auto-installed during pipeline bootstrap. Domain skills (e.g., HPC) live in `skills/library/` and are pulled in by the Researcher when relevant.\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n## CLI Reference\n\n| Command | Description |\n|:--------|:------------|\n| `ark new <name>` | Create project via interactive wizard |\n| `ark run <name>` | Launch the pipeline (auto-detects per-project conda env) |\n| `ark status [name]` | Score, iteration, phase, cost |\n| `ark monitor <name>` | Live dashboard: agent activity, score trend |\n| `ark update <name>` | Inject a mid-run instruction |\n| `ark stop <name>` | Gracefully stop |\n| `ark restart <name>` | Stop + restart |\n| `ark research <name>` | Run Gemini Deep Research standalone |\n| `ark config <name> [key] [val]` | View or edit config |\n| `ark clear <name>` | Reset state for a fresh start |\n| `ark delete <name>` | Remove project entirely |\n| `ark setup-bot` | Configure Telegram bot |\n| `ark list` | List all projects with status |\n| `ark doctor` | Diagnose a self-host install (envs, API keys, webapp) |\n| `ark cite-check <name>` | Verify project citations against DBLP / CrossRef |\n| `ark cite-search <query>` | Search academic databases for papers |\n| `ark audit <dir> [--repair]` | Verify delivered papers against the delivery contract |\n| `ark share create <name>` | Generate a share URL for a project |\n| `ark webapp install` | Install web dashboard service |\n| `ark access …` | Manage the (optional) Cloudflare Access allowlist |\n\n---\n\n## Dashboard\n\nidea2paper includes a web dashboard for managing projects, viewing scores, and steering agents — served from a single FastAPI process that also hosts the homepage (one port, one systemd unit). Beyond live phase badges and logs it gives you:\n\n- **Fair queueing** — every launch is capped at 2 dev + 2 review iterations; when the lanes are full, new projects queue with a position and an **estimated finish time**, and you get an email when the paper is done.\n- **Honest budgets** — the cost card shows the **provider-billed** total (the actual OpenRouter invoice, including deep research and figures) when available, and clearly labels estimates otherwise.\n- **Key-aware model picker** — only models you hold a key for are selectable; one OpenRouter key unlocks the whole list.\n- **Chat with your paper** — ask questions about a finished project, request targeted edits, or re-run a single experiment without a full iteration.\n- **Page-fit modes** — Relaxed / Balanced / Strict control how aggressively the paper is fitted to the venue page limit.\n\n### Configuration\n\nConfigured via `.ark/webapp.env` (auto-created on first `ark webapp` run). Set `SMTP_*` for magic-link login, `ALLOWED_EMAILS` / `EMAIL_DOMAINS` to restrict access, and optionally `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` for Google OAuth.\n\n### Management Commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|:--------|:------------|\n| `ark webapp` | Start the dashboard in the foreground (useful for debugging). |\n| `ark webapp release` | Tag the current code and deploy to the production worktree. |\n| `ark webapp install [--dev]` | Install and start as a `systemd` user service. |\n| `ark webapp status` | Show status of the systemd service. |\n| `ark webapp restart` | Restart the dashboard service. |\n| `ark webapp logs [-f]` | View or tail service logs. |\n| `ark webapp login <email>` | Print a fresh magic-link sign-in URL. |\n| `ark webapp publish` | Tag origin/main as the next release (tag-driven deploy). |\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Service Details (Prod vs. Dev)</strong></summary>\n\n| | Prod | Dev |\n|---|:-----|:----|\n| **Port** | 9527 | 1027 |\n| **Service Name** | `ark-webapp` | `ark-webapp-dev` |\n| **Conda Env** | `ark-prod` | `ark-dev` |\n| **Code Source** | `~/.ark/prod/` (pinned) | Current repository (live) |\n\n</details>\n\n### Hosting Idea2Paper for others?\n\nStanding up a **hosted, multi-tenant** Idea2Paper instance — host + web app setup,\nshared-prod team releases, and the GCP/AWS launcher setup that lets clients run\ncloud compute in their own accounts — is covered end-to-end in the operator\nrunbook:\n\n**→ [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)**\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Direct orchestrator invocation</strong></summary>\n\n```bash\npython -m ark.orchestrator --project myproject --mode paper --max-iterations 20\npython -m ark.orchestrator --project myproject --mode dev\n```\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Docker Usage</strong></summary>\n\n> [!IMPORTANT]\n> The idea2paper research runtime depends on scientific libraries that are most stable on x86_64. If you are building on an **Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3)** Mac, you must build for the `linux/amd64` platform.\n>\n> All idea2paper Dockerfiles and the `docker-compose.yml` are configured to force `linux/amd64` by default.\n\n**Running with Docker Compose**\n\n```bash\n# Start the web portal (builds the image automatically for amd64)\ndocker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build -d\n```\n\nThe web portal will be accessible at `http://localhost:9527`. All databases, configurations, and project data are persisted in a Docker named volume (`ark_data`).\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml logs -f webapp\n```\n\n**Configuration**\n\n```bash\ncp .ark/webapp.env.example .ark/webapp.env\n# Edit .ark/webapp.env with your credentials\n```\n\nThen uncomment the environment volume mapping in `docker/docker-compose.yml` under the `webapp` service:\n\n```yaml\n      - ../.ark/webapp.env:/data/.ark/webapp.env:ro\n```\n\n**Running Individual Jobs**\n\nUncomment the `job` service in `docker/docker-compose.yml`, then run:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml run --rm job \\\n  --project myproject \\\n  --project-dir /data/projects/<user-id>/myproject \\\n  --mode research \\\n  --iterations 10\n```\n\n*Pass required API keys (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) as environment variables.*\n\n**Running Standalone Containers**\n\n```bash\n# Build images (force amd64)\ndocker build --platform linux/amd64 -f docker/Dockerfile.webapp -t ark-webapp .\ndocker build --platform linux/amd64 -f docker/Dockerfile.job -t ark-job .\n\n# Run the Web Portal\ndocker run -d --name ark-webapp \\\n  --platform linux/amd64 \\\n  -p 9527:9527 \\\n  -v ark_data:/data \\\n  ark-webapp\n\n# Run a Research Job\ndocker run --rm -it \\\n  --platform linux/amd64 \\\n  -v ark_data:/data \\\n  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=\"sk-ant-...\" \\\n  ark-job \\\n  --project myproject \\\n  --project-dir /data/projects/myproject \\\n  --mode research\n```\n\n**Pushing to GCP**\n\n```bash\n# Push to Artifact Registry (recommended)\n./docker/push-gcp.sh --project [PROJECT_ID] --region [REGION] --repo [REPO] --build\n\n# Push to Legacy Container Registry (gcr.io)\n./docker/push-gcp.sh --project [PROJECT_ID] --legacy --build\n```\n\nThe `--build` flag automatically builds the images for `linux/amd64` even when running on macOS.\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n## Cloud Compute\n\nidea2paper's **v2 cloud architecture** decouples the *Control Plane* from the *Execution Plane*, enabling the full orchestrator to run on a **SkyPilot-provisioned cluster** while you interact with a lightweight local webapp. [SkyPilot](https://docs.skypilot.co) is now the only cloud compute path — it provisions across AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes from one abstraction, with spot instances, retries, and autostop teardown built in.\n\n**How it works:**\n1. The local webapp (or CLI) acts as a lightweight launcher — it runs `sky launch` to provision a remote **Orchestrator cluster**, syncs your project code (via SkyPilot `workdir`/`file_mounts`) and API keys, and triggers the orchestrator process.\n2. The **Orchestrator cluster** runs all high-level logic (Researcher, Planner, Writer, LaTeX, figures) remotely in a detached session.\n3. Experiments can run on the same orchestrator cluster or on a separate SkyPilot-provisioned GPU cluster (configurable independently).\n4. The orchestrator reports state home over the `/v1` control-plane API; the webapp streams logs and refreshes the Dashboard. The cluster self-terminates via **autostop** when the run completes (or after an idle window).\n\n> [!TIP]\n> Cloud credentials are encrypted at rest using your `SECRET_KEY`. Your keys are never logged or transmitted to third parties.\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Configuration Hierarchy</strong></summary>\n\nidea2paper uses a three-tier configuration model for cloud compute:\n1. **System Defaults**: Set in `webapp.env` — for GCP the central `CLOUD_GCP_PROJECT` holding the baked ARK image, plus `CLOUD_LAUNCHER_SA`, `CLOUD_LAUNCHER_SA_KEY`; for AWS `CLOUD_LAUNCHER_ROLE_ARN` + `CLOUD_LAUNCHER_AWS_PROFILE`; plus the shared `CLOUD_CONDA_ENV`.\n2. **Global User Defaults**: Set in the **Settings** panel (⚙️). These apply to all your projects.\n3. **Project Overrides**: Set during project creation or restart. These have the highest priority.\n\nThis hierarchy lets you define standard defaults once, while easily swapping to a powerful GPU instance (accelerators, spot) for a specific experiment.\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n### Enabling Cloud Compute via the Dashboard\n\n1. Open the **Settings** panel (⚙️ icon in the top navigation bar).\n2. Open the **Compute** tab.\n3. Enter your **GCP Project ID**, grant the shown `ark-launcher` service account the required roles on your project, then click **Verify access**. (No service-account key is uploaded — you delegate access to your own project via IAM. Operators: see [`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) §4.)\n4. Click **Save**.\n\nWhen creating a new project you can now independently select:\n- **Orchestrator Backend** — `skypilot` to run the control plane on a SkyPilot-provisioned cluster, or `local` to run it on the same machine as the webapp.\n- **Experiment Backend** — `skypilot` for GPU experiments, or `local` to run them on the Orchestrator cluster itself.\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Creating a Project</strong></summary>\n\nOnce cloud compute is configured, launch a project through the dashboard:\n\n1. Click **New Project** from the dashboard home.\n2. Fill in the research goal, target venue, and any additional instructions.\n3. Click **Submit** — the webapp generates a `config.yaml`, provisions the Orchestrator cluster via SkyPilot, syncs your project, and starts the run.\n\nThe generated `config.yaml` is stored at:\n\n```\n~/.ark/data/projects/<user_id>/<project_id>/config.yaml\n```\n\nYou can inspect or hand-edit this file at any time (e.g., to tune instance type or add `setup_commands`). Changes take effect on the next run or restart.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> If `PROJECTS_ROOT` is set in your `.ark/webapp.env`, the path above is replaced by `$PROJECTS_ROOT/<user_id>/<project_id>/config.yaml`.\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n### Cloud Provider Setup\n\nConfiguring the GCP / AWS / SkyPilot launcher — building the baked image,\ncreating the central `ark-launcher` identity, and wiring `webapp.env` — is an\n**operator** task done once per hosted instance. It's documented step-by-step,\nper cloud, in the deployment guide:\n\n**→ [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)** — §4 GCP · §5 AWS · §6 client onboarding · §8.4 `config.yaml` reference.\n\nIf you're *using* a hosted instance, you don't run any of that — just open\n**Settings → Compute**, enter your GCP project / AWS account, and click\n**Verify access** (above). Running on **Azure or Kubernetes**? SkyPilot handles\nthose too; configure that cloud's credentials per the\n[SkyPilot docs](https://docs.skypilot.co).\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Log Streaming & Re-attachment</strong></summary>\n\n- **Log Streaming** — the Orchestrator cluster streams logs home over the `/v1` control-plane API; the webapp polls it periodically to show live progress.\n- **State Sync** — the orchestrator checkpoints its `auto_research/` state to the control plane periodically, so the Dashboard UI stays current and the run survives VM loss.\n- **Re-attachment** — if you restart your local webapp, idea2paper detects the persisted SkyPilot cluster and re-attaches to the running process without re-provisioning.\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Cost Control</strong></summary>\n\n> [!WARNING]\n> Cloud clusters are billed by the hour. idea2paper leans on SkyPilot's built-in teardown to prevent runaway costs:\n>\n> - **Autostop-down** — every cluster is launched with an autostop-down window; if it sits idle past that window it **terminates itself**.
